The bridge, named after Sir Michael Otedola, who served as the ninth Governor of Lagos State between 1992 and 1993, has become notorious because of the fatal vehicle crashes and devastating tanker explosions.
Though many commuters and locals tend to attribute the frequent, horrific accidents on Otedola Bridge to a bad omen, spiritual covenants, or blood-sucking demons, safety and structural experts have said the frequent mishaps are entirely due to a combination of severe structural engineering defects, human error, and regulatory failures on the part of the government.
The latest incident occurred Monday, Oct. 19, 2026, when a diesel-laden tanker plunged from the bridge and caught fire, leaving at least two adult men with second- and third-degree burns as the tanker was engulfed in fire under the bridge.
The Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA), Dr Olufemi Damilola Oke-Osanyintolu, who confirmed the incident, said the victims were evacuated for further medical treatment.
Oke-Osanyintolu said the fallen tanker was conveying 33,000 litres of diesel, adding that the fire was contained through the coordinated efforts of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, its response team, the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) and the Lagos State Ambulance Service.
“The Agency is pleased to inform the public that the fire explosion resulting from a fallen tanker conveying thirty-three thousand litres of diesel under the Otedola Bridge has been successfully curtailed,” the statement reads.
According to LASEMA, its paramedics and the Lagos State Ambulance Service provided pre-hospital care to the two victims, stabilising them at the scene before evacuating them for further treatment in the hospital.
The agency added that the fallen tanker would be recovered and evacuated from beneath the bridge after the damping exercise to ensure the area’s safety.
“The State Government is happy to announce that traffic flow along the Otedola Bridge corridor has been fully restored,” the statement said.
The LASEMA boss reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to protecting lives and property through prompt emergency response and collaboration among relevant agencies.
The Controller General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Mrs Margaret Abimbola Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 16:09 hours reporting a fire involving a tanker conveying petroleum products from a depot.
According to her, the tanker fell between the inward and outward sections of the Otedola Bridge, resulting in a fire. ‘’Upon receipt of the distress call, firefighters from the Alausa and Ikeja Fire Stations were immediately mobilised to the scene. The responding teams arrived at 16:16 hours and commenced firefighting operations. ‘’Through the prompt and coordinated intervention of the firefighters, the fire was successfully extinguished. Damping-down operations are ongoing to eliminate residual hotspots and prevent possible re-ignition.
‘’Further details regarding the circumstances surrounding the incident, its cause, and any casualties or property damage will be communicated as verified information becomes available.’’
The ill-fated bridge continues to take its toll on commuters and residents living along that axis. Civil engineers have identified the steep gradient as the root cause of the accident on the bridge. The bubble usually bursts when heavily loaded petrol tankers and container trucks try to ascend the sharp incline, thereby placing massive strain on their poorly serviced engines and mechanical systems. At this point, the chips are normally down when they lose momentum, roll backwards, or experience sudden brake failure.
Another problem is overloading of poorly maintained trucks. Past incidents have revealed that many articulated heavy-duty vehicles plying the interstate route are severely overloaded and structurally unfit for the road.
The risk of avoidable accidents increases when these substandard trucks encounter a steep slope, and their mechanical components fail, causing them to tip over, spill volatile petroleum products, and trigger catastrophic explosions.
The latest incident follows several crashes recorded on or around the bridge over the past three years.
Available records show that the first major, widely reported catastrophe on the bridge happened on June 28, 2018, when a petroleum tanker exploded and killed 12 people and burnt 54 vehicles. This accident is widely documented as the incident that brought the bridge widespread national and international notoriety as a major accident black spot.
Sept. 12, 2023: A wheat-laden truck fell from the bridge, killing one occupant. May 24, 2024: Lagos State Ambulance Service records documented a fatal hit-and-run incident near Otedola Bridge. The service’s record said responders found a corpse when they arrived. Jan. 7, 2025: Four trucks were involved in a series of crashes around the bridge. One person died, and three others were injured. March 11, 2025: A gas-laden articulated truck fell and exploded, damaging vehicles and nearby buildings. The National Emergency Management Agency initially reported one death and four injuries, while later reports put the death toll at two.
April 7, 2025: A sedan fell from the bridge, with reports indicating that its four occupants were injured. Oct. 30, 2025: A heavily loaded truck reportedly suffered brake failure and crashed into other vehicles, leaving one person injured. Dec. 8, 2025: Two occupants of an unregistered vehicle died after it collided with a heavily loaded trailer at Otedola Bridge, inward Berger. The trailer driver reportedly fled the scene. Jan. 9, 2026: A truck rammed into two cars. No casualties were reported. Jan. 23, 2026: On this day, multiple crashes involving heavy-duty trucks killed one driver and caused severe traffic congestion. March 11, 2026: Yet another incident involving a coloured person, with the truck tumbling during a recovery operation, spilling two containers onto the road and causing major traffic disruption. No deaths were reported in that incident.
April 22, 2026: On this day, a dispatch rider died after a collision with a heavy-duty truck at Otedola Bridge, inward to the Lagos State Government Secretariat.
Sept. 16, 2026: Five vehicles, including SUVs and commercial vehicles, were involved in a crash. No deaths were reported.
In the wake of these accidents the Lagos state government in its usual reactive statements promised to restrict tanker movements and strengthen roadworthiness checks for heavy-duty vehicles. As it is it suffice to say that nothing concrete has ever been done by the government to avert a repeat of the road carnages.
